clue.text: West-Indian accountant faces ridicule

parts.note: CA stands for chartered accountant
to rib someone is to tease or mock them

explanation.surface: A Caribbean bookkeeper is met with mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces' is a link word placing the accountant before the ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribs are an indigenous people of the Lesser Antilles, so a Carib is a native of the islands.

clue.text: Cheat sore competitor

parts.note: to con is to cheat or swindle
tender means painful to the touch

explanation.surface: A rival who swindles is left aching.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is someone competing for a prize or title, a rival.

clue.text: Go back for right exit

parts.note: an egress is a way out

explanation.surface: Someone retreats looking for the way out on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To regress is to return to an earlier state or move backwards.

clue.text: Let off steam if sore

explanation.surface: Someone vents their anger if they are hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' is a link word between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Water at boiling point gives off vapour, and someone furious is said to seethe; separately, a boil is an inflamed pus-filled swelling on the skin.

clue.text: Bit of a game for the Shadow Home Secretary

explanation.surface: A piece of a pastime is likened to a senior opposition politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was the Labour Party's Shadow Home Secretary in the mid-1990s; a jackstraw is one of the sticks in the game of spillikins (pick-up sticks).
explanation.definitionFit: A jackstraw is a single stick in pick-up sticks, and the Labour politician of that name held the opposition's home-affairs brief.

clue.text: Friendly spirit master found in Chopin's piano pieces

indicators.note: found in means the master's letter sits inside the rearranged letters
the composer's works are pieces, but here pieces means the letters are broken up

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree

explanation.surface: A warm fellowship is detected in the composer's piano works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' looks like musical works but signals the anagram of CHOPINSPIANO, into which 'found in' places M.
explanation.definitionFit: Companionship is fellowship, the friendly feeling between people who spend time together.

clue.text: South American needs Persian capital

parts.note: USA, the United States of America, stands in for American

explanation.surface: A Latin American traveller needs to visit the chief city of Persia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one phrase but splits into S and USA; 'needs' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Susa was an ancient city of Elam and a royal seat of the Achaemenid Persian kings.

clue.text: Contacted everyone indebted

annotationWithheld.why: Contacted everyone indebted (7): EACH inside RED, but 'indebted' must give both RED (in debt = in the red) and the container signal 'in', one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Spent money in Japan going after clothes

indicators.note: going after means the yen follows the clothes in the answer

parts.note: wear is clothing, as in menswear
Y is the symbol for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: Someone splashed out cash in Tokyo after buying an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent' looks like a verb about money but is the adjective meaning exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent describes someone tired out, which is what weary means.

clue.text: Egg-flip and gin sling are bracing for a chippy

parts.note: egg-flip is egg-nog, and nog is also spelt nogg

indicators.note: to sling something is to toss it about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe suggests eggnog and a gin cocktail make a tonic for a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sling' turns GIN into ING. A gin sling is a real drink, which hides the anagram signal; a chippy is British slang for a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nogging is the short timber or brick infill used to stiffen a framed wall, work done by a carpenter.

clue.text: Visiting the opera is dirt cheap

explanation.surface: An evening at the opera costs next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: heading out to hear singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, attending a performance means heading off for some music; idiomatically the phrase means being sold for a very low price.

clue.text: Mother's got expensive Italian make-up

parts.note: Ma is mother, with the possessive s
cara is Italian for dear or expensive

explanation.surface: Mum has bought a pricey Italian cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a cosmetic applied to darken the eyelashes.

clue.text: Always the number-one woman to Rex

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A leading lady is forever devoted to a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, a synonym for constantly.

clue.text: Minister takes half a dozen by motor

parts.note: six is VI in Roman numerals
a motor is a car

explanation.surface: A clergyman squeezes six people into his automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'by' are link words joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, a minister of the Church of England.

clue.text: Hailing a freight barge

parts.note: a hoy is a heavy flat-bottomed boat for carrying cargo

explanation.surface: Someone calls out to a cargo vessel on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahoy is the sailor's cry used when calling to another ship.

clue.text: The bread is mine, thank you

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone claims the loaf as theirs, with polite thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; 'mine' looks like the possessive but is the colliery.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, slightly leavened bread from the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Shot warm-hearted naval NCO

indicators.note: hearted says the word for warm becomes the heart, sitting inside the other piece

parts.note: PO is a petty officer, a naval non-commissioned officer
hot is a stronger warm

explanation.surface: A kindly naval petty officer has been shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warm-hearted' reads as kindly, but splits into HOT and the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a photograph, as in a holiday snap.

clue.text: Made out and became famous

explanation.surface: Someone perceived something and won renown.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense works as in 'distinguished himself', winning fame.
explanation.definitionFit: To have discerned something is to have spotted it apart from its surroundings; and someone who stood out in a field earned eminence.

clue.text: Vision appearing to visionary tourist

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision
a seer is a prophet or visionary

explanation.surface: A vision appears to a mystic who is visiting the sights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sightseer visits famous places, which is what a holidaying tourist does.

clue.text: To offer free tailoring is useless

explanation.surface: A tailor who works without charge is pronounced worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is read whimsically: a tailor making clothes at no charge would measure and suit you gratis.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, the phrase means providing a suit's fitting gratis; as an idiom it means being of no practical use.

clue.text: Disagree about how to go off parade

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over how to leave a military parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link word between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarrel is to fall out, and the same phrase is the drill order dismissing soldiers from ranks.

clue.text: Men love, but they detest at leisure. (Byron)

definitions.text: Men love, but they detest at leisure. (Byron)

parts.words: Men love, but they detest at leisure. (Byron)
parts.note: a line from Byron's Don Juan with two words missing after love, contrasting hasty affection with slow-burning hatred

explanation.surface: Byron observes that men fall for someone quickly but take their time hating.
explanation.walkthrough: A missing-words clue: the full line from Don Juan supplies the two words that fill the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means hurriedly, the opposite of the leisurely pace of hatred in the line.

clue.text: Complaint made by many of advanced years

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, taken loosely as many
elderly people are old

explanation.surface: An ailment suffered by lots of elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold is a common minor illness, and complaint is a word for an ailment.

clue.text: Manage to go round a small wood

indicators.note: to go round means the word for manage surrounds the small letter

parts.note: to cope is to manage
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone tries to manage a walk round a little woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' looks like part of the definition 'a small wood' but gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small group of trees, a thicket or little wood.

clue.text: Some rented a charming Russian cottage

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers took a delightful little house in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a country house or villa in Russia, often used in summer.

clue.text: About to smack a little girl

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
to smack is to hit

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of slapping a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Chit is a dated, slightly dismissive word for a young or pert girl.

clue.text: Permit letters 1 and 22 to be transliterated

indicators.note: transliterated means written in another order of characters, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the first letter of the alphabet is A
the twenty-second letter of the alphabet is V
is is a form of the verb to be

explanation.surface: Authorisation is given for clue answers 1 and 22 to be written in another script.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 and 22' look like grid references (CARIB, DACHA) but are positions in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official endorsement permitting entry to a country.

clue.text: Sadly, a childless young woman

indicators.note: childless means without a son, so the S for son is dropped

parts.note: a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Regrettably, a young woman has no children.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the usual abbreviation for son; removing it from LASS leaves LAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of grief, used like regrettably or unfortunately.

clue.text: Stipulation is accepted by militant Sinn Feiner

indicators.note: accepted by means the word is is taken inside the other piece

parts.note: a Provo is a member of the Provisional IRA, associated with Sinn Fein

explanation.surface: A condition is agreed to by an Irish republican hardliner.
explanation.walkthrough: Provo was the everyday name for a member of the Provisional IRA, the militant wing of Irish republicanism.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition attached to an agreement, the same as a stipulation.

clue.text: Sleep is disturbed in a long coat

indicators.note: disturbed sleep is broken up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's slumber is interrupted while wearing a full-length coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a long cloak or fur-lined coat, worn especially by women or hussars.

clue.text: Disaffected paper chief quaffed rum

indicators.note: quaffed means drank down, so the editor takes the other word inside

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A disgruntled newspaper editor knocked back some rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' wants to be the drink; here it is the British adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Estranged describes someone alienated, no longer friendly or close.

clue.text: Promise made by Cornish auditor

parts.note: Cornwall is in the South West of England, abbreviated SW
an ear is the organ that hears, an auditor

explanation.surface: A pledge given by an accountant from Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' wants to be an accountant; it is the listener, the ear. Cornwall is England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to vow or give one's word, a verb sense of promise.
